clue.text: Organising tour frequently bores musician

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece goes inside the musician's name

parts.note: Sting is the English rock singer and bassist

indicators.note: frequently points to every other letter of tour being taken

parts.note: alternate letters, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Planning a heavy concert schedule wears a rock star down.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting is the English rock musician; 'bores' reads as boring an audience but means drilling into his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting things out is arranging them in order, the same activity as organising.

clue.text: Instrument made of tin a butcher held up

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: to butcher is to murder

explanation.surface: A drum fashioned from a tin can, raised aloft by a butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its lower head.

clue.text: Ruling, and expecting to have no power

indicators.note: to have no means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: expecting means pregnant
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A monarch on the throne who also happens to be expecting a baby but lacks real authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant who rules in her own right.

clue.text: Inspire independent mob rule from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means only some letters show up, every other one

parts.note: first and third letters
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A free spirit occasionally stirs up anarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue someone is to fill them with a feeling or idea, much as inspiring does.

clue.text: Spurs goal almost leads to defensive substitution

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word taken as written

indicators.note: leads means the opening letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur nearly score, prompting a defensive change.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Goads and spurs are both verbs meaning urges on or provokes into action.

clue.text: There's no getting round it, I'm no longer trendy!

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
passé means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to the fact that they have gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation with no way past or around the obstacle.

clue.text: Unrecognisable gin mixed with tonic and a dash of orange

indicators.note: mixed as in a cocktail means the letters of the drinks are stirred together
a dash of means just a little, the first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: gin and tonic with a splash of orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means in disguise, with true identity concealed so as not to be recognised.

clue.text: Wage officer in team prays for a reorg

indicators.note: a reorg is a reorganisation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company's staff hope for a restructure.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official responsible for paying salaries to staff or troops.

clue.text: Constituency housing for Spanish coastal town

indicators.note: housing means containing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a parliamentary seat is a constituency
por is Spanish for for

explanation.surface: A political district providing homes for Spaniards on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaport is a town with a harbour where ships load and unload.

clue.text: Somewhat influential things, philosophically speaking

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Ideas with a modest impact, in the language of philosophers.
explanation.definitionFit: Entia is the Latin plural of ens, a being or existing entity in philosophy.

clue.text: Rebalancing, with no indefinite numbers reinterpreted from maths work

indicators.note: reinterpreted means the remaining letters are read in a new order
with no tells us letters standing for the numbers are dropped from the word

parts.note: N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number; two of them here

explanation.surface: Fixing an equation after the unknowns have been removed, as a maths exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes both Ns from REBALANCING, leaving REBALACIG; 'reinterpreted' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebraic describes something arising from algebra, a branch of mathematical study.

clue.text: Positive votes won't ultimately provide the reason for an uprising?

parts.note: yeas are votes in favour

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word won't

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A political puzzle: yes votes fail to explain why a revolt broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: The uprising is bread dough rising, not a rebellion; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast produces gas that makes dough swell, so it causes bread to rise.

clue.text: Fish sandwiches staff put round plates

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between its parts, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: eels are fish

indicators.note: put round means the word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: staff wrap fish in sandwiches and hand plates around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' looks like crockery but is a verb: to plate is to coat with a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean coating a surface with a hard decorative or protective layer.

clue.text: Family member has a look around for cereal

parts.note: gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: around tells us the short phrase is turned backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Grandma checks the cupboard for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo, meaning look or behold, is an old word much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is a breakfast mix of baked oats, nuts and fruit, a type of cereal.

clue.text: Freethinking artist into cavorting with the Hollywood elite

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the A-list are the top celebrities

explanation.surface: An unconventional painter frolicking with film stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artist' looks like the anagram fodder beside 'cavorting', but the jumbled word is 'into'; the A-list is Hollywood's top tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationalist relies on reason rather than religious authority, which is what free thought means.

clue.text: After working, other people stop improving

parts.note: on means functioning, switched on
them means people other than us
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Once employed, others call a halt to their progress.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering health, getting better after illness.

clue.text: Maintain food can be turned away

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert
table means food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Claims that food may be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Avertable describes something able to be averted, prevented or deflected.

clue.text: Trademark protecting a piece of headgear

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes around the other letter

explanation.surface: A brand name shields a hat design from imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tam is a soft round woollen cap worn in Scotland, a type of hat.

clue.text: Runner's trouble with green pants

definitions.note: Runner's is read as runner is, the 's being the link

parts.note: a mess is a trouble or predicament

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete's problem with green trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means rubbish or poor, an anagram signal here rather than trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger is a courier or runner who carries messages.

clue.text: Skirt has to be returned as I don't think much of it

definitions.text: I don't think much of it

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to skirt or border something is to hem it

explanation.surface: A disappointed shopper sends a skirt back, unimpressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Meh is an interjection expressing indifference or lukewarm feeling about something.

clue.text: Brand fronted by fashionable old actress

indicators.note: fronted by means the second piece goes in front

parts.note: hep is an old slang variant of hip, fashionable
to brand is to burn a mark on

explanation.surface: A clothing label promoted by a trendy veteran film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey and Katharine Hepburn were both famous film actresses of the classic Hollywood era.

clue.text: Crime drama seeing a person shot, badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A TV thriller in which someone is gunned down and badly wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sopranos is the HBO television series about a New Jersey Mafia family.

clue.text: VIP taking in cool international city

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside

parts.note: a nob is a posh important person
to air is to cool, as in airing a room

explanation.surface: A celebrity attends a relaxed global metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, a large East African city.

clue.text: Most simple pastry dishes covered in pepper

indicators.note: covered in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to pepper is to dot or sprinkle
pies are pastry dishes

explanation.surface: A cook judges the plainest pies to be those sprinkled with pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means foolish, so the dopiest person is the most simple-minded.

clue.text: US narcs regularly lost supplies of drugs

parts.note: the DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: American drug agents habitually mislay seized narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug deals are sales or transactions of narcotics.

clue.text: Name of bread roll accompanying thin stew occasionally

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters are used, here every other one

parts.note: first and third letters
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A recipe naming a roll served with watery stew.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll. 'occasionally' takes alternate letters of 'thin stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: To baptise is to give a name, especially at a christening.

clue.text: A place you go to pursue black bear

indicators.note: to pursue means to come after, so the following pieces sit behind

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
loo is British slang for the toilet, the place you go

explanation.surface: A spot to visit before chasing a black bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British for toilet. Baloo is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloo is the easy-going brown bear who teaches Mowgli in The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Spy network given external training?

indicators.note: given external means another piece goes outside it, as an outer shell

parts.note: PT is physical training
a LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: An intelligence ring sent abroad for instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an agent secretly placed in an organisation to gather information.

clue.text: Sharp knife wound admitted to A&E

indicators.note: admitted to means taken inside, as a patient into hospital

parts.note: A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department; its letters are used
a cut is a wound from a blade

explanation.surface: A stabbing victim is taken into the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means keen or pointed, as in an acute angle or acute pain.

clue.text: Notice a pipe providing isolated source of fresh water

parts.note: a bill is a poster or notice
a bong is a water pipe for smoking

explanation.surface: A sign points to a pipe that supplies water to a remote spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian pool or backwater cut off from a river.

clue.text: Nurse is knocked back, having to go without a date

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
to die is to go, pass away

explanation.surface: A nurse is rejected and must leave with no partner for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface date sounds romantic; the definition is about adjourning with no day fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for adjourning indefinitely, with no day appointed to resume.

clue.text: Peripheral figure revealed by storyteller on podcast

parts.note: something revealed is out in the open

indicators.note: a podcast is heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a liar tells stories

explanation.surface: A fringe character exposed by a narrator on an audio show.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a person or data point lying far from the main group.
